newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran assembly gets Khatami compromise cabinet list.
newsitem.headline: Iran assembly gets Khatami compromise cabinet list.

text.p: Iran's moderate new President Mohammad Khatami on Tuesday submitted his cabinet choices to the conservative-dominated parliament in his first key test in office.

In a letter to the parliament, Khatami presented his list of 22 ministers which diplomats and analysts saw as one of compromise on the politically sensitive posts of foreign affairs, intelligence and defence but a clear signal on domestic portfolios where the Shi'ite cleric promised change.
Parliament speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri said the 270-seat assembly would start debating the nominations next Tuesday and give its verdict in a vote of confidence the following day.

Analysts said the nomination of conservative cleric and parliament deputy Qorbanali Dorri Najafabadi as intelligence (internal security) minister was an important concession by the reformist president to his opponents in parliament.
Dorri Najafadadi would replace Ali Fallahiyan against whom Germany last year issued an arrest warrant for allegedly ordering political killings in Berlin. Iran denied the charges.
Khatami named United Nations ambassador Kamal Kharrazi to replace Ali Akbar Velayati as foreign minister.

Kharrazi is seen by diplomats as a loyal technocrat unlikely to herald major changes in foreign policy, the realm of supreme leader Ayatollah Khamenei. Khamenei has rejected the possibility of a thaw in relations with the United States.
First reaction from conservative newspapers suggested that Khatami may face obstacles to secure approval for some of his appointment, analysts said.
The evening daily Resalat on Tuesday criticised Khatami for not negotiationing with parliament before submitting his list.
"How can they vote for a minister who they do not find trustworthy, competent, committed and efficient?" it added.

Khatami's list included no women despite expectations after his landslide election win in May that he would appoint at least one woman to the cabinet for the first time since the 1979 Islamic revolution. Newspapers said he might name a female vice-president.
Hossein Namazi was chosen for the economy and finance portfolio, Bijan Namdar Zanganeh switched to the oil ministry from energy, and navy chief Rear-Admiral Ali Shamkhani was named to defence.
Ataollah Mohajerani, named as minister of culture and Islamic guidance, is Khatami's potentially most controversial choice, analysts said.
Mohajerani has faced increasingly sharp criticism from conservatives after he advocated direct talks with the United States in 1990 and pressed for more cultural freedoms.
The cultural ministry decides which books, films, music and other social pastimes are allowed in the Islamic republic.
"Khatami has sent a signal that he will honour his election mandate of bringing social justice and civil law," said a Western diplomat who expected deputies to challenge Mohajerani.

"It points to Khatami pressing for discreet but important changes on the domestic scene, particularly in regard to social policy, while leaving alone foreign and security matters in the hands of his more conservative opponents," said one diplomat.
Khatami's ability to put in place a cabinet of his own choosing is seen as vital to the reforming scope and tone of his four-year administration.
One diplomat said nominations for the three central posts of foreign affairs, intelligence and defence would be quickly accepted by parliament conservatives.
"Each of them stands for the status quo, promising little change in the short-term," the diplomat said.
Abdollah Nouri, named as interior minister, held the same post from 1989 to 1993. He is a leader of a leftist cleric group that has moved to a more centrist position in recent years.
"He is a reformist who will work like a bulldozer. He will change most provincial governors and mayors and will have a crucial role in the next parliament elections," a diplomat said.

Three of the proposed ministers retained portfolios they held under former president Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani. They are Issa Kalantari at agriculture, Hossein Kamali at labour and and Esmail Shoushtari at the justice ministry.

Two ministers proposed in the new cabinet were also carried over from Rafsanjani's cabinet but were given new portfolios -- new oil minister Zanganeh and Gholamreza Shafei, who switched to the industry portfolio from the cooperatives ministry.
Khatami was sworn in as president on August 4, sealing a huge political victory against Nateq-Nouri.
The 54-year-old moderate Shi'ite cleric was supported by the vast majority of Iran's young, women and middle class voters on a platform of more social freedoms and economic justice.
